78th Creative Arts Emmys Night Two: ‘Widow’s Bay’ Dominates, ‘DTF St. Louis’ Wins Big, ‘The Pitt’ and ‘Pluribus’ Make a Race for Drama

Karen Peterson September 6, 2026

The 78th Emmys continued tonight with a ceremony honoring the creative artists in the drama, comedy, TV movies and limited or anthology series.

In what will undoubtedly serve as a preview for next week’s Primetime Emmys broadcast, freshman series Widow’s Bay dominated the comedy categories with guest actress Betty Gilpin overtaking five Hacks guest stars and previous winner Jamie Lee Curtis of The Bear. Apple TV’s new horror comedy series, a favorite to win Comedy Series next week, was the top winner of the night scoring eight total prizes including production design, costuming, music, casting, and cinematography. Meanwhile, Hacks, which ended its five-season run in May, came in with 17 nominations in the evening, taking home one award for picture editing.

It was a big night to celebrate comedy and its enduring power when the Television Academy also unveiled the inaugural Legacy Award, recognizing the long-lasting impact of the beloved comedy classic I Love Lucy, “for its profound and generational impact on the television industry and audiences around the globe.” The beloved show, which launched Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz Jr into stardom, premiered on CBS 75 years ago.

Over in the drama lineup, the race is clearly a two-way match between reigning champion The Pitt and newcomer Pluribus which took home four Emmys apiece tonight. With its overall 25 nominations, HBO’s medical drama is still well-positioned to repeat in drama series next week, but the Apple TV freshman drama series is going to put up a good fight.

The other major matchup comes in the limited or anthology series lineup between HBO’s DTF St. Louis and Netflix’s second season of Beef, which won three years ago. Both are strong contenders, though DTF goes home tonight with six awards over Beef‘s three, with the HBO series winning both supporting acting categories as well as writing and directing. It will be tough for Beef to overcome that deficit.

There was a bittersweet celebration when Rob Reiner posthumously won the award for Guest Actor in a Comedy Series for his appearance in season four of The Bear. Presenter Wendi McClendon-Covey invited a standing ovation saying, “It’s appropriate to stand for this one. I know we all wish Rob could be here tonight.”

Two cancelled shows also leave as winners tonight with Prime Video’s Spider-Noir taking five awards and Apple TV’s campy soap Palm Royale nabbing two. Apple TV overall had a big night with their other new series Margo’s Got Money Troubles winning three as well.

Now that the two-night Creative Arts awards have concluded, an edited version of the show will air on FXX Saturday, September 12 at 8 p.m. The Primetime Emmy awards will be broadcast live on NBC and stream on Peacock Monday, September 14 at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Emmy winner Mariska Hargitay will host.

 
Here is the complete list of Night Two winners:

Juried Awards – Animation (Previously announced)
Outstanding Individual Achievement in Animation
Eyes of Wakanda – “Into the Lion’s Den”
Genndy Tartakovsky’s Primal – “Kingdom of Sorrow”
Genndy Tartakovsky’s Primal – “Vengeance of Death”
The Mighty Nein – “Mote of Possibility”
Star Wars: Visions – “The Duel: Payback”

Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series: Shailene Woodley, Paradise
Outstanding Fantasy/Sci-Fi Costumes: Fallout (“The Strip”)
Outstanding Period Costumes: Palm Royale (“Maxine Is Ready to Single Mingle”)
Outstanding Contemporary Costumes for a Series: Margo’s Got Money Troubles (“Grudge Match”)
Outstanding Contemporary Costumes for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie: Beef, (“All the Things We’re Never Going to Have”)
Outstanding Guest Actor in a Drama Series: Ernest Harden Jr., The Pitt
Outstanding Production Design For A Narrative Contemporary Program (One Hour Or More): Pluribus (“Grenade”)
Outstanding Production Design For A Narrative Period Or Fantasy Program (One Hour Or More): Fallout (“The Wrangler”)
Outstanding Production Design For A Narrative Program (Half-Hour): Widow’s Bay (“Lodging”)
Outstanding Casting For A Comedy Series: Widow’s Bay
Outstanding Casting For A Drama Series: The Pitt
Outstanding Casting For A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette
Outstanding Choreography For Scripted Programming: Palm Royale (“Comin’ Home Baby”/”I Want to Be a Cowboy’s Sweetheart”/”I Had a Ball”)
Outstanding Stunt Performance: A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (“In the Name of the Mother”)
Outstanding Stunt Coordination For Comedy Programming: Spider-Noir
Outstanding Stunt Coordination For Drama Programming: The Boys
Outstanding Contemporary Hairstyling: Margo’s Got Money Troubles (“Buddies”)
Outstanding Period Or Fantasy/Sci-Fi Hairstyling: Bridgerton (“The Waltz”)
Outstanding Contemporary Makeup (Non-Prosthetic): Margo’s Got Money Troubles (“Grudge Match”)
Outstanding Period Or Fantasy/Sci-Fi Makeup (Non-Prosthetic): Palm Royale (“Maxine Drinks Martinis Now”)
Outstanding Prosthetic Makeup: The Pitt (“9:00 P.M.”)
Outstanding Picture Editing For A Drama Series: Pluribus (“We Is Us”)
Outstanding Picture Editing For A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: DTF St. Louis (“No One’s Normal. It Just Looks That Way from Across the Street”)
Outstanding Picture Editing For A Multi-Camera Comedy Series: Leanne (“Having Big Feelings”)
Outstanding Picture Editing For A Single-Camera Comedy Series: Hacks (“Hacks (Finale)”)
Outstanding Animated Program: South Park (“Sermon on the ‘Mount”)
Outstanding Character Voice-Over Performance: Julie Andrews, Bridgerton
Outstanding Sound Editing for a Comedy Or Drama Series (Half-Hour) And Animation: Widow’s Bay (“What to Expect On Your Trip”)
Outstanding Sound Editing For A Limited Or Anthology Series, Movie Or Special: Beef (“It Will Stay this Way and You
Will Obey”)
Outstanding Sound Editing For A Comedy Or Drama Series (One Hour): Spider-Noir (“The Man in the Mask”)
Outstanding Sound Mixing For A Comedy Or Drama Series (Half-Hour) And Animation: Widow’s Bay (“What to Expect On Your Trip”)
Outstanding Sound Mixing For A Comedy Or Drama Series (One Hour): Pluribus (“We Is Us”)
Outstanding Sound Mixing For A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: Beef (“It Will Stay this Way and You
Will Obey”)
Outstanding Title Design: Spider-Noir
Outstanding Supporting Actor In A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: David Harbour, DTF St. Louis
Outstanding Special Visual Effects In A Season Or A Movie: Stranger Things
Outstanding Special Visual Effects In A Single Episode: Spider-Noir (“Nightmare on a Gurney”)
Outstanding Cinematography For A Series (Half-Hour): Widow’s Bay (“Our History”)
Outstanding Cinematography For A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: DTF St. Louis
Outstanding Cinematography For A Series (One Hour): Spider-Noir (“Step Into My Office”)
Outstanding Original Music And Lyrics: The Pitt (“12:00 P.M.”/Song Title: “Need Someone”)
Outstanding Original Main Title Theme Music: Pluribus
Outstanding Music Supervision: Widow’s Bay (“Beach Reads”)
Outstanding Music Composition For A Series (Original Dramatic Score): Widow’s Bay (“Our History”)
Outstanding Music Composition For A Limited Or Anthology Series, Movie Or Special (Original Dramatic Score): The Beast in Me
Outstanding Supporting Actress In A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: Linda Cardellini, DTF St. Louis
Outstanding Directing For A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: Steven Conrad, DTF St. Louis
Outstanding Writing For A Limited Or Anthology Series Or Movie: Steven Conrad, DTF St. Louis
Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series: Rob Reiner, The Bear
Outstanding Guest Actress in a Comedy Series: Betty Gilpin, Widow’s Bay
Outstanding Movie: Remarkably Bright Creatures

Karen Peterson fell in love with movies when she was six months old and her parents couldn't find a babysitter on date night, so they brought her along. Her love for film has taken her to film festivals including Sundance, LAFF, AFI, Middleburg and the Hamptons, as well as the press rooms of the Spirit Awards, the Golden Globes, and the Oscars. She is also the cohost of the Citizen Dame and Watch and Talk podcasts, as well as a frequent guest on any show that will let her talk about Tom Cruise.
